docs.title: CERIDWEN
docs.text:
CERIDWEN fits galaxy spectral energy distributions to infer stellar populations, dust properties, nebular emission and star formation histories. It accepts photometry, spectra and emission-line fluxes, separately or in a joint fit.

The forward model uses JAX to combine stellar populations, apply dust attenuation and emission, add nebular continuum and lines, and account for intergalactic absorption. It then projects the spectrum into the observed frame at the galaxy's redshift. The model is differentiable, and inference can run on a CPU or GPU.

docs.title: Model components
docs.text:
• Star formation histories on a lookback-time grid, using non-parametric continuity (logsfr_ratios) or parametric forms supplied as transforms.
  • Constant metallicity or a metallicity history (zh_const).
  • Sampled [α/Fe] with CSPBasis_afe and the aMIST + C3K grid.
  • Kriek & Conroy diffuse dust, power-law birth clouds and 12 attenuation laws, including Calzetti, SMC, LMC, Gordon+03 SMC bar and Reddy+15.
  • Dust emission from Draine & Li (2007) or THEMIS templates.
  • Nebular continuum and emission lines from FSPS CLOUDY grids.
  • Madau (1995) IGM attenuation, with optional damping wing and damped Ly-α absorption through MadauDampingDLA.
  • Broadening from stellar and gas velocity dispersions and the instrumental LSF, accounting for the SSP library resolution.

Fits can include noise rescaling, jitter, calibration polynomials, an outlier mixture and a GP for correlated spectral residuals. Emission-line fluxes and calibration coefficients can be marginalised analytically. Inference options are nested sampling, NUTS, VI-preconditioned NUTS and MAP optimisation. PostProcess computes derived quantities, posterior predictions and figures.

docs.text:

docs.title: Related projects
docs.text:
CERIDWEN's internal filter-convolution and attenuation-curve code comes from Benjamin D. Johnson's sedpy, through the JAX rewrite sedpy_jax. It also follows sedpy's AB photon-counting conventions. Neither package is a dependency.

Maintainer: Amanda Stoffers, Kavli Institute for Cosmology, University of Cambridge, aas208@cam.ac.uk

docs.title: Fitting [α/Fe]
docs.text:
The α-enhanced grid uses FSPS v4.0, aMIST isochrones and C3K spectra, with [α/Fe] ∈ {−0.2, 0.0, +0.2, +0.4, +0.6}. It lets you fit [α/Fe] alongside metallicity. [α/Fe] can help constrain the formation timescale, although it is degenerate with total metallicity.

SSPDataAfe and CSPBasis_afe extend SSPData and CSPBasis with an [α/Fe] axis and interpolation. They omit the nebular arguments and inherit the SFH weights, dust, projection, flux scaling and cosmology.

docs.title: The grid
docs.text:
Download the grid by name. The 612 MB file is cached and verified with SHA-256. To build it yourself, compile python-fsps from source with AFE_FLAG=1 against the FSPS v4.0 data tree. Check both settings before building.

import jax.numpy as jnp
from ceridwen.ssps import fetch_grid, SSPDataAfe
from ceridwen.csp import CSPBasis_afe
from ceridwen import Cosmology

ssp = SSPDataAfe.load(fetch_grid("amist_c3k_hr_krou_afe"))
ssp.display()                       # (n_afe, n_Z, n_age, n_wave) = (5, 13, 107, 10992)

csp = CSPBasis_afe(ssp, lookback_time=jnp.linspace(0.0, 12.0, 9),
                   cosmo=Cosmology.planck18(), zh_const=True, verbose=False)

theta = {
    "lookback_time":      jnp.linspace(0.0, 12.0, 9),
    "sfh":                jnp.exp(-jnp.linspace(0.0, 12.0, 9) / 1.0),
    "logzsol":            jnp.array([-0.3]),   # = [Fe/H] on an aMIST grid
    "afe":                jnp.array([0.4]),    # [α/Fe]: re-partitions that Z
    "tau_pow":            jnp.array([0.3]),
    "alpha_pow":          jnp.array([-1.0]),
    "diffuse_tau_kc":     jnp.array([0.2]),
    "diffuse_dust_index": jnp.array([0.0]),
}
wave, fnu = csp.wave, csp.get_spectrum(theta)   # rest-frame Lsun/Hz per Msun
print(csp)                                      # grids, [Fe/H] axis, Z_sun, parameters
i = int(jnp.argmin(jnp.abs(wave - 5500.0)))
print(f"{fnu.shape[0]} pixels, L_nu(5500 A) = {float(fnu[i]):.3e} Lsun/Hz per Msun")

amist_c3k_hr_krou_afe uses M. J. Park's alpha-MC C3K high-resolution SSPs (MIST v2.5 + C3K v2.3) and a Kroupa IMF. Between 3000 and 9000 Å, the spectra are resampled at λ/Δλ = 6000 per pixel. The two-pixel resolution limit is therefore R ≈ 3000; ssp.display() reports it. The native FSPS metallicity axis is log10 Z = [Fe/H] + log10(0.0185), so logzsol represents [Fe/H].

docs.title: What differs from CSPBasis
docs.text:
• theta["afe"] is interpolated linearly between adjacent grid planes. It supports jit, grad, vmap and all samplers.
  • All [α/Fe] planes share the FSPS AFE_FLAG=1 [Fe/H] axis. Total metallicity is derived as logzsol_total = logzsol + log10(1 - x + x 10^[α/Fe]), with x = 0.687490 for MIST v2.5, GS98.
  • There is no nebular model because α-enhanced CLOUDY grids are unavailable. Lines observations raise an error. The basis reads from $SPS_HOME only when add_dust_emission=True.
  • CSPBasis_afe requires an α-aware 4-D grid. Passing a solar-scaled 3-D grid raises a TypeError directing you to CSPBasis. When constructing a grid by hand, pass ssp_afe= as a keyword.
  • A prior that includes both logzsol > +0.25 and [α/Fe] > +0.4 raises an error at construction. FSPS supplies the same isochrone file at [Fe/H] = +0.5 for [α/Fe] = +0.4 and +0.6. display() identifies this cell.
  • The grid has no surviving-mass table. Use fitSED(..., mfrac=False) and report formed mass.
  • Sampling afe uses interpolation weights in the [α/Fe] contraction rather than constructing a flux plane for each sample. Vectorised evaluation uses roughly the same memory as evaluation without afe. For jit(vmap(csp.get_spectrum)) on the CPU, XLA's compile-time memory_analysis reports temporary memory of 0.005 GB at W = 1, 0.002 GB at W = 80 and 0.011 GB at W = 400 for this grid. The basis also stores two float32 copies of the flux cube, each 306 MB.

examples/demo_afe_quiescent.py fits a quiescent galaxy with [α/Fe] and a sampled spectrophotometric normalisation.

docs.title: AGN models
docs.text:
CSPBasis(..., agn=AGNConfig(...)) adds AGN emission. The default agn_mode="corrected" normalises and attenuates the components as described below. Modes "fsps" and "prospector" reproduce the corresponding implementations, subject to the differences listed in the comparison sections. Mode "cigale" follows CIGALE's SKIRTOR and polar-dust conventions.

Omitting agn= preserves existing predictions byte for byte, as checked by scripts/bit_identity_check.py. The additional AGN2 components are disabled by default and do not change AGNConfig() predictions until enabled.

from ceridwen import CSPBasis, Cosmology
from ceridwen.agn import AGNConfig

csp = CSPBasis(ssp, lookback_time=lb, zh_const=True, add_dust=True, add_neb=True,
               add_dust_emission=True, cosmo=Cosmology.planck18(),
               agn=AGNConfig())                       # corrected mode, torus + disc + lines
csp = CSPBasis(ssp, ..., agn=AGNConfig(agn_mode="fsps"))         # FSPS add_agn_dust
csp = CSPBasis(ssp, ..., agn=AGNConfig(agn_mode="prospector", dust4_type=1))

agn=True means AGNConfig(). A string such as agn="fsps" sets AGNConfig(agn_mode="fsps"). CSPBasis_afe accepts the same argument. See examples/agn_demo.py for an example.

docs.title: Components and parameters
Fitting the AGN line width
docs.text:
agn_eline_sigma is the Gaussian dispersion in km/s for the 23 AGN narrow lines. Corrected mode combines it with the instrumental width at each line as sqrt(agn_eline_sigma² + sigma_inst²). Profiles are evaluated on all pixels by SpectralProjector.setup_agn_lines. Gradients remain finite down to 1e-3 km/s (tests/agn/test_eline_sigma.py).

Fixed values, transforms and prior support must lie in (0, 2000] km/s, using the default Kinematics.sigma_max. Invalid values raise an error at setup. These lines use Richardson+14 narrow-line ratios. For broad-line emission, use AGNConfig(blr=True) and blr_sigma, described below.

Only a spectrum resolving AGN lines provides a useful width constraint. Integrated Lines fluxes are independent of width; photometry depends on it mainly near filter edges. SedModel warns if a width prior is supplied without a spectrum, without unmasked AGN-line pixels, or when instrumental sigma exceeds three times the prior's upper bound at every AGN line. Fix the width in these cases:

transforms = {"agn_eline_sigma": lambda th: jnp.array([100.0])}   # and no prior on it

The instrumental sigma is sigma_inst = c / (2.3548 R_FWHM):

R_FWHM sigma_inst [km/s] resolves (sigma_inst <= 3 x prior upper edge) for an upper edge >= 30 4244 1415 km/s 100 1273 424 km/s 300 424 141 km/s 1000 127 42 km/s 2700 47 16 km/s

Passing this check does not establish that the width is measured. A prism at R ≈ 100 with Uniform(50, 500) passes because 1273 < 3 × 500, yet the posterior remains prior-dominated. In the tests below, the grating constrained the width and the prism did not.

The CPU recovery test used scripts/agn_injection_recovery.py --spec grating|prism at z = 3 with JADES-like photometry and a noiseless rest-frame 3600–6900 Å spectrum, assigned continuum S/N 20 per pixel. Corrected mode included nebular emission. Input values were agn_elum=3e-3, agn_eline_sigma=250 and sigma_gas=60. These, stellar parameters and continuum AGN parameters were fitted jointly with nested sampling and slice_kernel="lanes":

parameter truth grating, R 1000 (num_live 400): median, 16-84 % in 2.5-97.5 % prism, R 100 (num_live 100): median, 16-84 % in 2.5-97.5 % agn_elum 0.003 0.0033 (0.00312 to 0.00348) yes 0.00368 (0.00306 to 0.00435) yes agn_eline_sigma 250 252 (248 to 255) yes 267 (141 to 378) yes sigma_gas 60 60.4 (58.1 to 62.8) yes 139 (62.6 to 224) yes log_fagn -0.523 -0.417 (-0.61 to -0.231) yes -0.517 (-0.654 to -0.249) yes agn_tau 20 28 (14.8 to 46.2) yes 21.4 (11.9 to 46) yes log_fagn_bbb 0 -0.0036 (-0.0178 to 0.0124) yes 0.0397 (-0.025 to 0.107) yes logmass 10 9.956 (9.934 to 9.979) NO (97.5 %: 9.999) 9.931 (9.9 to 9.974) yes logzsol -0.5 -0.543 (-0.585 to -0.493) yes -0.558 (-0.659 to -0.478) yes diffuse_tau_kc 0.4 0.4 (0.387 to 0.417) yes 0.439 (0.377 to 0.502) yes

The ratio of posterior to prior standard deviation for agn_eline_sigma was 0.029 with the grating and 0.85 with the prism. Grating line parameters were recovered to a few percent. logmass was just outside its 95% interval: the 97.5% quantile was 9.999 with 400 live points and 9.991 with 100. The input has χ² = 0, and the best 100-live-point sample had χ² = 0.9. The mass offset reflects marginalisation over SFH directions rather than a missed likelihood peak. Since agn_elum is per formed mass, it is strongly anti-correlated with logmass (−0.92). The script writes posteriors to sigma_<spec>[_nl400].npz.

Gas-width degeneracy. AGN and star-forming emission share wavelengths such as Hβ, [O III], Hα, [N II] and [S II]. Each observed profile combines Gaussians of widths sqrt(sigma_gas² + sigma_inst²) and sqrt(agn_eline_sigma² + sigma_inst²). Separating them depends on their relative fluxes and line ratios.

For the prism, both widths were weakly constrained: sigma_gas was 139 (+85/−76) km/s for an input of 60, and the AGN posterior/prior width ratio was 0.85. The grating recovered agn_eline_sigma=252 (+3/−4) and sigma_gas=60.4 (+2.4/−2.3) km/s, with correlation −0.17. Different line ratios helped distinguish the two contributions.

The fixed Richardson+14 'a42' ratios and gas-dependent CLOUDY ratios also constrain agn_elum when widths are unresolved. The prism fit gave 3.68e-3 [3.06e-3, 4.35e-3] for an input of 3e-3. Interpret AGN emission using the line ratios as well as the profiles.

docs.title: FSPS, Prospector and corrected modes
docs.text:
"fsps" "prospector" "corrected" (default) reproduces FSPS add_agn_dust Prospector AGNSSPBasis + AGNSpecModel — torus resampling sps_setup.f90: log-log with FSPS's float32 tiny30, locate edges fake_fsps.agn_torus: argmin edges, log-log positive rows only, zero outside, renormalised so that the torus carries exactly fagn * L_bol on any grid agn_tau outside [5, 150] clamped (flat likelihood) extrapolated linearly (can go negative) clamped (flat likelihood) torus screen galaxy diffuse curve none galaxy diffuse curve disc screen (no disc) diffuse curve x dust4 screen diffuse curve x dust4 screen IGM on the AGN none (FSPS adds the torus after igm_absorb) Prospector's fake_fsps.add_igm (17 Lyman lines, no metal term) the CSP's IGM, like every other component AGN lines painted with Prospector's painter (no instrument, no dust, no IGM); photometry as delta functions same as fsps nebular painter with agn_eline_sigma (instrument included), the galaxy's diffuse dust and the IGM at each line; photometry through the model grid like the nebular lines energy balance no no absorbed AGN light (continuum and lines) re-emitted by DL07 when add_dust_emission=True

Without dust emission, absorbed AGN light is removed from the output, as is absorbed stellar light. FSPS and Prospector modes do not support AGN energy balance and reject agn_energy_balance=True. In those modes, AGN lines require add_neb=True because the Prospector profiles are placed only near nebular lines. Corrected mode does not require a nebular model to add AGN lines.

docs.title: Comparison with FSPS and Prospector
docs.text:
Reference files use python-fsps 0.5.0 (libfsps 05b5e55) and prospect 91f8e13. scripts/agn_reference/make_refs.py writes them to tests/reference/agn/*.npz; comparisons are in tests/agn/.

test what result A1 fsps-mode torus vs python-fsps spec(fagn) - spec(0): fagn {1e-3, 0.1, 1, 3} x agn_tau {5, 7.5, 10, 40, 150} x dust2 {0, 0.5, 1.5} x z {0, 2, 7} max rel 1.7e-8, inside FSPS's own cancellation floor (REF's rule); a float64 numpy port of FSPS agrees to the same floor A2 prospector-mode torus vs fake_fsps.agn_torus, agn_tau 1-300 (extrapolation) max rel 3.1e-14 A3 disc + dust4 screen vs agnssp_basis.get_spectrum (140 configs, dust_type 0/2/4/6, dust4_type 0/1, z 0/6) max rel 5.7e-14 A4 AGN lines vs AGNSpecModel (agn_eline_sigma 50, 300) luminosities exact; spectrum 1.2e-13 of peak; Lines 8.9e-18; photometry 1.7e-16 with sedpy's curves (6e-5 with CERIDWEN's vendored NIRCam curves, a filter-data difference) A5 whole model vs python-fsps + AGNPolySpecModel (z = 3, 15 NIRCam + MIRI bands) torus spectrum 1.7e-14 (Prospector's L_bol fed in); disc spectrum 1.7e-14 in shape; full-CSP AGN-only photometry = Prospector's x the galaxy scalars to 1.1e-3 (the filter-curve term, the same on the galaxy)

The whole-model A5 comparison depends on differences in stellar L_bol, the 5500 Å disc normalisation and filter curves. For its BPASS SFH, CERIDWEN/Prospector ratios were 0.8515 for L_bol, 0.8300 for disc normalisation and 0.99447 for flux normalisation from cosmology. Accounting for these factors leaves the filter-curve difference.

In the referenced Prospector version, AGNSSPBasis passes fagn and agn_tau to python-fsps, whose Fortran default add_agn_dust=1 adds a torus. Python-fsps cannot disable that default. AGNSSPBasis then adds fake_fsps.agn_torus, producing 1.39–1.90 times the torus-only photometry. CERIDWEN's Prospector mode reproduces the single torus term. The test tests/agn/test_a5_whole_model.py records this difference.

docs.title: Corrected-mode checks
docs.text:
test result B1 resampled torus integrates to 1 on any grid abs(sum(T w) - 1) <= 2e-15 for every tau node B2 node exactness, clamping, no negative flux, no NaN for tau in [0.1, 1e4] pass B3 fagn = fagn_bbb = agn_elum = 0 equals AGN off byte-identical, all modes, all eight kernels, a/Fe, wavelength_support=True, Photometry + Spectrum + Lines B4 linear in fagn, fagn_bbb, agn_elum exact in the float64 AGN term; to float32 rounding in the predictions B5 L_torus = fagn x L_bol (screen off) rtol 1e-10 B6 energy balance absorbed AGN light (continuum + lines) re-emitted; conserved to DL07's own self-absorption loss, 4.6e-7 of the absorbed light, the same as the stellar path B7 IGM order (corrected vs fsps at z = 8) the difference is the AGN light blueward of Ly-alpha times the IGM: 0.36 % (tau 5) to 1.33 % (tau 150) of L_AGN B8 jit, vmap (W = 64, 100), grad finite gradients in every AGN key; vmap = loop to float32 reordering B9 marginalize_elines with AGN lines refused at setup

On a dense grid, integrating the log-log interpolated Nenkova+08 SEDs gives 0.989–0.996 times the trapezoidal integral of the original nodes. Corrected mode renormalises to fagn * L_bol; FSPS mode retains the FSPS normalisation. The resulting difference is 0.4–1.1%.

docs.title: AGN2 components: SKIRTOR, polar dust, NLR and BLR
docs.text:
These four AGNConfig switches are disabled by default:

from ceridwen.agn import AGNConfig
agn = AGNConfig(agn_mode="corrected",            # or "cigale"
                torus_model="skirtor16",         # SKIRTOR torus + its disc (replaces Nenkova+08)
                polar_dust=True, polar_law="smc",  # CIGALE polar dust ("smc", "calzetti", "gaskell")
                nlr_model="feltre16",            # Feltre+16 narrow lines (replace the a42 ratios)
                blr=True)                        # broad H I lines
component theta keys (default) meaning source SKIRTOR 2016 torus + disc fagn (0), skirtor_t (7), skirtor_pl (1), skirtor_q (1), skirtor_oa (40), skirtor_i (30) amplitude (below); tau_9.7 {3..11}, p, q {0..1.5}, opening angle [deg, equator to torus edge] {10..80}, inclination [deg, 0 = face-on] {0..90}; AGNConfig(skirtor_R=10/20/30) static (default 20) Stalevski+12, +16 templates as CIGALE's skirtor2016 uses them (Schartmann 2005 disc, delta 0; cigale 29cb909f) polar dust polar_ebv (0.03), polar_temp (100 K), polar_emis (1.6) E(B-V) of the polar screen; grey body T, beta (lambda_0 = 200 um) CIGALE skirtor2016.py (Yang+20, +22) Feltre+16 NLR agn_elum (0), agn_eline_sigma (100), nlr_logu (-2.5), nlr_logz (0), nlr_alpha (-1.7), nlr_xid (0.3), nlr_lognh (3) L_Hbeta,NLR [L_sun] per formed M_sun; sigma [km/s]; log U_S [-5, -1]; log Z/Z_sun [-2.18, +0.66] (Z_sun = 0.01524); alpha [-2, -1.2]; xi_d [0.1, 0.5]; log n_H [2, 4] public NEOGAL grid (AGN_NLR_nebular_feltre16.tar.gz), 17 of its 20 lines (N V 1240, [Si III] 1883, Si III] 1888 are not in the FSPS line list); [O II] 3726+3729 sits on [O II] 3726 as in the a42 table BLR blr_lum (0), blr_sigma (1500) L_Halpha,BLR [L_sun] per formed M_sun, before attenuation; Gaussian sigma [km/s] (FWHM = 2.35482 sigma; support [400, 5000]) 8 H I lines (H alpha-delta, Pa alpha-delta), Case B (Storey & Hummer 1995 via PyNeb), T = 1e4 K, n_e = 1e4: H alpha / H beta = 2.847 (ceridwen/agn/data/blr_caseB_T1e4_ne1e4.csv)

Interpolation is multilinear in the tabulated variables, using log line ratios for the NLR. Values are clamped to grid edges. Fixed values outside a grid produce a setup warning; priors extending outside it raise an error.

SKIRTOR (227 MB) and NLR tables are supplied separately. The repository scripts scripts/agn2/build_skirtor_h5.py and build_nlr_h5.py write skirtor2016.h5 and nlr_feltre16.h5 to $CERIDWEN_AGN_DATA, which defaults to ~/.ceridwen/agn/. Missing files raise an error at construction with setup instructions. Dependent tests skip with "MISSING ...: did NOT run". The SKIRTOR and Feltre+16 redistribution licences have not been checked.

docs.title: CIGALE extinction curves
docs.text:
Below 100 nm, polar dust uses CIGALE's extFun_SMC.dat, extFun_MRN.dat and extFun_Gaskel04.dat from pcigale/sed_modules/curves/ at commit 29cb909f. These CeCILL-2.0 files are not bundled with CERIDWEN. Install them in $CERIDWEN_AGN_DATA (default ~/.ceridwen/agn/):

python -m ceridwen.agn.fetch --from /path/to/cigale   # a CIGALE checkout or installed pcigale; no network
python -m ceridwen.agn.fetch --download               # from gitlab.lam.fr, through the system curl

From Python, use ceridwen.agn.fetch_grids(from_cigale=...) or fetch_grids(download=True). Each SHA-256 must match the reference table used by the comparison tests; differing files are not written. Manual copies may use the CIGALE names or the older cigale_extFun_*.txt names. Missing or changed curves raise a construction error when polar_dust=True. Tests requiring missing curves are skipped.

The following combinations are unsupported:

  • AGN2 switches in "fsps" or "prospector" mode.
  • SKIRTOR with the Temple disc or dust4_type=1, since SKIRTOR includes its own disc and uses polar dust for its nuclear screen.
  • polar_dust=True without SKIRTOR.
  • In "cigale" mode, the Nenkova torus, Temple disc, dust4 screen or a42 lines. With SKIRTOR, galaxy dust is required because fagn is defined relative to its luminosity. This mode also rejects fesc_geometry="picket", since that luminosity is calculated using screen geometry. A fagn prior must remain below 1.
  • marginalize_elines=True with narrow or broad AGN lines.

docs.title: agn_mode="cigale" and "corrected"
docs.text:
"cigale" "corrected" fagn (SKIRTOR) CIGALE's fracAGN = P / (P + L_dust,gal): P = torus + polar-dust luminosity, L_dust,gal what the galaxy's dust absorbs from stars and nebular emission (CIGALE's dust.luminosity); must be < 1 P / L_bol,* (as the Nenkova torus); CIGALE's fracAGN is reported as frac_agn_cigale galaxy dust on the AGN none (CIGALE adds the AGN after its dust modules) the diffuse curve on the disc, torus, polar re-emission, NLR and BLR energy balance none what the galaxy's dust absorbs from the AGN goes to DL07 (with add_dust_emission=True) polar dust CIGALE: the disc extinguished only for a type-1 view (i <= 90 - oa); the re-emitted luminosity is the angle-averaged absorption of the face-on disc; disc, torus and grey body renormalised together the same 4 pi accounting; CIGALE's Calzetti k (negative above ~3.1 um) clipped at 0 resampling onto the model grid CIGALE's np.interp of L_lambda, 0 outside the template grid log-log between positive template points, scaled to the template's own integral (pixels independent of the model grid's extent) NLR attenuation none (the Feltre NLR is not a CIGALE component; CIGALE's unreleased nebular_AGN would apply the polar screen) galaxy diffuse curve at each line BLR blr_lum with the Case-B table, polar-dust transmission at each line (CIGALE's nebular_AGN convention); CIGALE's own BLR scaling (ionising photons x covering factor, Cloudy tables with H alpha / H beta = 46 at its defaults) is not reproduced polar (or dust4) transmission x galaxy curve at each line; what the polar screen removes is not re-emitted (CIGALE re-emits only disc light) line profile Gaussian in ln lambda (CERIDWEN's painter); CIGALE's AGN lines are Gaussian in lambda: they differ at order sigma/c (4.7e-4 of the peak at FWHM 800 km/s, 4.1e-3 at 7000), same area same IGM after the AGN (CIGALE's redshifting module acts on every contribution) the same

With SKIRTOR, PostProcess returns extras["agn"]["frac_agn_cigale"] in both modes; it equals fagn in "cigale" mode. CIGALE's agn.* information is stored as cigale_<name>, including accretion power, intrinsic L_nu at 2500 Å viewed at 30°, L_6um, L_12um and disc, torus and polar luminosities. It also returns L_dust_gal, L_skirtor_disk, L_skirtor_dust and L_polar_ir.

docs.title: Priors
docs.text:
The following choices are used in the AGN2 configuration, with NLR priors following BEAGLE-AGN (Vidal-Garcia+24):

  • In "cigale" mode, use fagn ~ Uniform(0, 0.99). In corrected mode, use log_fagn ~ Uniform(-5, log10 3).
  • Without mid-IR coverage, fix skirtor_t=7, skirtor_pl=1, skirtor_q=1 and skirtor_oa=40. Use skirtor_i ~ Uniform(0, 90).
  • Use polar_ebv ~ Uniform(0, 1).
  • For the NLR, use nlr_logu ~ Uniform(-4, -1.5) and nlr_logz ~ Uniform(-2.18, 0.24). Fix nlr_xid=0.3, nlr_alpha=-1.7 and nlr_lognh=3, which are degenerate with log U and amplitude.
  • Use blr_sigma ~ LogUniform(400, 3000) km/s. This corresponds to the cited JWST broad-Hα FWHM range of 890–6279 km/s. Only a resolved spectrum constrains this width; integrated line fluxes do not.

docs.title: Line amplitudes are independent of the AGN continuum
docs.text:
agn_elum for Richardson+14 or Feltre+16 narrow lines and blr_lum for broad lines are luminosities per formed solar mass. They do not depend on fagn, fagn_bbb or the continuum. FeltreNLR.line_luminosity returns agn_elum * R_line(theta), AGNLines returns agn_elum * ratio and BroadLines returns blr_lum * ratio_halpha. The CSP multiplies these by the SFH's formed mass sum(W) and 10**logmass.

This allows broad or narrow AGN lines with fagn=fagn_bbb=0. Use priors to restrict this if required by your model. Without energy balance, amplitudes are constrained by line emission and only weakly by photometry that does not resolve it. With agn_energy_balance=True, line light absorbed by galaxy dust is re-emitted by DL07, adding an IR constraint.

For scale, the AGN2 notes quote galaxy nebular Hβ luminosities of roughly 1e-3–1 L_sun per formed M_sun. This range has not been recomputed here. An agn_elum of 1 can therefore be comparable to the galaxy's entire nebular Hβ luminosity.

Tying line amplitudes to the AGN continuum would require an ionising-photon integral, a Case-B or CLOUDY conversion and a covering factor. It would also change parameter registration, the linear-amplitude tests and the golden configuration.

docs.title: NLR ratios use a separate Feltre+16 grid
docs.text:
The NLR uses the five Feltre, Charlot & Gutkin (2016) axes: nlr_logu, nlr_logz, nlr_xid, nlr_lognh and nlr_alpha (nlr.py:54–60). nlr_alpha is the UV slope used to generate that grid. It is independent of the fitted disc: SKIRTOR has no slope parameter and Temple+21 has only amplitude fagn_bbb. NLR ratios therefore do not respond to the fitted continuum's luminosity or shape.

A continuum-coupled NLR would require a disc model with a slope matching the grid axes and the photon-rate normalisation described above. A transform could then tie nlr_alpha to that slope.

docs.title: The BLR does not depend on inclination
docs.text:
BroadLines has parameters blr_lum and blr_sigma (blr.py:112). Its attenuation includes the nuclear screen, either polar dust or the dust4 power law, and in corrected mode the galaxy's diffuse curve. PolarDust.transmission depends on polar_ebv, without an inclination term, as in CIGALE.

The SKIRTOR disc receives polar attenuation only at type-1 inclinations, skirtor_i <= 90 - skirtor_oa, while broad lines receive it at every inclination. The model does not hide the BLR automatically for a type-2 view. If broad lines should be absent, constrain blr_lum accordingly.

Inclination-dependent BLR obscuration would require a covering or attenuation function, a decision about re-emitting hidden light and a new golden configuration. It would also change the interpretation of blr_lum as observed broad-Hα luminosity.

docs.title: There is no X-ray or corona component
docs.text:
The model has no X-ray component or alpha_ox normalisation. It cannot predict an X-ray flux or use X-ray measurements to constrain the AGN.

The disc templates do extend below the Lyman limit:

  • The Temple+21 template ends at 91 Å. Corrected mode sets shorter-wavelength flux to zero rather than extrapolating a constant F_nu (disk.py:98–100).
  • The SKIRTOR parametric disc starts at 8 Å (skirtor_disk / schartmann2005_disk, skirtor.py:113–116) and includes EUV emission on its template grid.

The SSP model grid's shortest wavelength and IGM transmission determine which of this emission reaches a prediction.

An X-ray extension would need a component and normalisation convention, such as CIGALE's alpha_ox relation to 2500 Å disc luminosity. It would also require extending the model grid, IGM and filter projection below the SSP wavelength limit, with a new golden configuration.

docs.title: Outputs and compatibility
docs.text:
• In PostProcess, spectra_model and spectra_observed include AGN continuum; spectra_intrinsic and spectra_dustfree exclude it. Consequently, A_V = 2.5 log10(dustfree/full) includes the AGN contribution. spectra_agn contains AGN continuum alone. extras["agn"] returns L_bol_star, L_absorbed and, with energy balance, mdust for dust heated by the AGN. Stellar dust mass is not reported. LUV and MUV include AGN emission. AGN narrow lines appear only in per-observation predictions.
  • Result files record mode, components, energy balance and template/table hashes in /model@csp_config["agn"]. check_model_against_result reports differences in AGN configuration.
  • Line marginalisation rejects models with AGN lines because the free fluxes would absorb those lines. Disable them with AGNConfig(lines=False) to marginalise, also leaving the BLR disabled when applicable.
  • Supplying fagn without agn= produces an unknown-key warning and adds no AGN. Enable the component when constructing the CSP.
  • AGN calculations use dense operations without scatter-adds, and the CPU comparison tolerances also apply on GPU.

def with_stellar_mass(self, mass, *, source):
    """Return a copy carrying the surviving stellar-mass table ``mass`` (shape
    ``ssp_flux.shape[:-1]``, M_sun per M_sun formed) with its provenance ``source``."""
    import dataclasses as _dc
    if not source:
        raise ValueError("with_stellar_mass: pass source= (where the masses come from)")
    return _dc.replace(self, ssp_stellar_mass=self._checked_stellar_mass(mass),
                       stellar_mass_source=str(source), schema_version=self._schema_version())

def with_resolution(self, *, sigma_v=None, segments=None, source=None):
    """Return a copy carrying a library resolution curve from exactly one of ``sigma_v`` (km/s on ssp_wave, NaN where unknown) or ``segments``."""
    import dataclasses as _dc
    from .library_resolution import sigma_v_from_segments
    if (sigma_v is None) == (segments is None):
        raise ValueError(
            "with_resolution: pass exactly one of sigma_v= or segments=")
    if segments is not None:
        sigma_v = sigma_v_from_segments(
            np.asarray(self.ssp_wave), segments)
    return _dc.replace(
        self,
        ssp_resolution=np.asarray(sigma_v, dtype=np.float64),
        resolution_source=(str(source) if source is not None else None),
    )

def display(self, *, return_str: bool = False, file=None):
    """Print (or return as str when ``return_str``) a summary of the grid and its provenance."""
    import sys as _sys

    wave  = np.asarray(self.ssp_wave)

    def _fmt(v, na="—"):
        return na if v is None else str(v)

    size = float(np.asarray(self.ssp_flux).nbytes)
    for unit in ("B", "KB", "MB", "GB", "TB"):
        if size < 1024.0 or unit == "TB":
            size_str = f"{size:.1f} {unit}"
            break
        size /= 1024.0

    lines = [
        self._display_title,
        "-" * 66,
        "provenance",
        f"  isochrones (isoc_type)   : {_fmt(self.isoc_type)}",
        f"  spectral library         : {_fmt(self.spec_library)}",
        f"  IMF (imf_type)           : {_fmt(self.imf_type)}",
        f"  FSPS version             : {_fmt(self.fsps_version)}",
        f"  schema version           : {_fmt(self.schema_version)}",
        f"  recorded wave_min/max    : {_fmt(self.wave_min)} / {_fmt(self.wave_max)}",
        f"  build kwargs             : {self.fsps_kwargs or '{}'}",
        "grids",
    ] + self._display_grid_lines(size_str)
    if self.ssp_resolution is None:
        lines += ["  library resolution       : MISSING "
                  "(cannot be saved; attach with with_resolution)"]
    else:
        res = np.asarray(self.ssp_resolution, dtype=np.float64)
        fin = np.isfinite(res)
        if fin.any():
            cov_lo = wave[fin].min(); cov_hi = wave[fin].max()
            lines += [
                f"  library resolution       : sigma_v "
                f"[{res[fin].min():.1f}, {res[fin].max():.1f}] km/s over "
                f"[{cov_lo:.0f}, {cov_hi:.0f}] AA "
                f"({100.0 * fin.mean():.0f}% of pixels; NaN elsewhere)",
            ]
        else:
            lines += ["  library resolution       : all-NaN "
                      "(unknown everywhere; no subtraction will occur)"]
        if self.resolution_source:
            lines += [f"  resolution source        : {self.resolution_source}"]
    if self.stellar_mass_refused:
        lines += ["  surviving stellar mass   : REFUSED at load (mfrac and the surviving "
                  "mass unavailable; everything else works)",
                  f"    {self.stellar_mass_refused}"]
    elif self.ssp_stellar_mass is None:
        name = published_grid_name(self.chash)
        which = (f"the published grid {name!r} has none yet" if name is not None
                 else "no ssp_stellar_mass table")
        lines += [f"  surviving stellar mass   : not available ({which}): mfrac and the "
                  "surviving mass are unavailable; everything else works"]
    else:
        m = self.ssp_stellar_mass
        lines += [f"  surviving stellar mass   : [{m.min():.4g}, {m.max():.4g}] M_sun per "
                  f"M_sun formed ({self.stellar_mass_source or 'source not recorded'})"]
    lines += self._display_note_lines()

    txt = "\n".join(lines)
    if return_str:
        return txt
    print(txt, file=file or _sys.stdout)
    return None

def save(self, filename):
    """Write grids, resolution curve and provenance attrs to HDF5 (overwrites); raises ValueError if ``ssp_resolution`` is None."""
    if self.ssp_resolution is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__}.save(): this grid carries no library "
            f"resolution curve (ssp_resolution is None).  "
            f"{self._schema_label} files require one — attach it with "
            "with_resolution(segments=...) or with_resolution(sigma_v=...) "
            "before saving."
        )
    with h5py.File(filename, 'w') as f:
        f.create_dataset('ssp_lgmet',      data=np.array(self.ssp_lgmet))
        f.create_dataset('ssp_lg_age_gyr', data=np.array(self.ssp_lg_age_gyr))
        f.create_dataset('ssp_wave',       data=np.array(self.ssp_wave))
        f.create_dataset('ssp_flux',       data=np.array(self.ssp_flux))
        f.create_dataset('ssp_resolution',
                         data=np.asarray(self.ssp_resolution,
                                         dtype=np.float64))

        f.attrs['description']        = 'FSPS SSP interpolation grids'
        f.attrs['units_lgmet']        = self._units_lgmet()
        f.attrs['units_lg_age_gyr']   = 'log10(age/Gyr)'
        f.attrs['units_wave']         = 'Angstrom'
        f.attrs['units_flux']         = 'L_sun Hz^-1 M_sun^-1'
        f.attrs['units_resolution']   = 'sigma_v [km/s]; NaN = unknown'
        self._save_extra(f)
        if self.ssp_stellar_mass is not None:
            f.create_dataset('ssp_stellar_mass',
                             data=np.asarray(self.ssp_stellar_mass, dtype=np.float64))
            f.attrs['units_stellar_mass'] = ('M_sun surviving (stars + remnants) per '
                                             'M_sun formed, per SSP')
            if self.stellar_mass_source is not None:
                f.attrs['stellar_mass_source'] = str(self.stellar_mass_source)
        if self.resolution_source is not None:
            f.attrs['resolution_source'] = str(self.resolution_source)

        for key in ('schema_version', 'isoc_type', 'spec_library',
                    'fsps_version'):
            val = getattr(self, key)
            if val is not None:
                f.attrs[key] = str(val)
        if self.imf_type is not None:
            f.attrs['imf_type'] = int(self.imf_type)
        if self.wave_min is not None:
            f.attrs['wave_min'] = float(self.wave_min)
        if self.wave_max is not None:
            f.attrs['wave_max'] = float(self.wave_max)
        f.attrs['fsps_kwargs_json'] = json.dumps(self.fsps_kwargs or {})
        f.attrs['log10_zsun'] = float(self.log10_zsun)
        f.attrs['zsun_nominal'] = float(self.zsun_nominal)
        if self.axis_meaning is not None:
            f.attrs['axis_meaning'] = str(self.axis_meaning)
        f.attrs['chash'] = str(self.chash)
        if self.refused_cells:
            f.attrs['refused_cells_json'] = json.dumps([list(c) for c in self.refused_cells])

@classmethod
def load(cls, filename, flux_dtype=None, zsun=None):
    """Load a grid from HDF5; raises ValueError if the file lacks ``ssp_resolution``. ``flux_dtype`` casts the flux cube on read.
    ``zsun`` supplies the grid's solar metallicity when it is neither recorded in the file nor in ``grid_metadata.CHASH_TABLE``."""
    arrays, _extra, meta = cls._read_h5(filename, flux_dtype=flux_dtype)
    return cls(**arrays, **meta, zsun=zsun)

Build a grid from the SPS backend, attach the library resolution curve and record provenance.

Only library/IMF-defining kwargs (LIBRARY_IMF_KWARGS) are accepted. The resolution curve is the element-wise maximum of the 2-pixel sampling floor of ssp_wave and resolution_segments (if given, which then require resolution_source). Raises ValueError otherwise.

Source code in ceridwen/ssps/ssp_data.py 
@classmethod
def from_fsps(cls, save_to: Optional[str] = None,
              resolution_segments=None,
              resolution_source: Optional[str] = None,
              **fsps_kwargs) -> "SSPData":
    """Build a grid from the SPS backend, attach the library resolution curve and record provenance.

    Only library/IMF-defining kwargs (``LIBRARY_IMF_KWARGS``) are accepted.
    The resolution curve is the element-wise maximum of the 2-pixel sampling
    floor of ``ssp_wave`` and ``resolution_segments`` (if given, which then
    require ``resolution_source``). Raises ValueError otherwise.
    """
    if resolution_source is not None and resolution_segments is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "from_fsps(): resolution_source was given without "
            "resolution_segments.  The sampling-floor provenance is "
            "recorded automatically; a source note only accompanies "
            "explicit library-LSF segments."
        )
    if resolution_segments is not None and resolution_source is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "from_fsps(): resolution_segments were given without "
            "resolution_source.  Cite where the LSF numbers come from "
            "(e.g. resolution_source='MILES FWHM 2.54A "
            "(Falcon-Barroso et al. 2011)') — uncited resolution "
            "numbers must not ship in a released grid."
        )
    from .library_resolution import combined_sigma_v, combined_source
    data = collect_ssp_data_wrapper(**fsps_kwargs)
    sigma_v = combined_sigma_v(np.asarray(data.ssp_wave),
                               segments=resolution_segments)
    data = data.with_resolution(
        sigma_v=sigma_v, source=combined_source(resolution_source))
    if save_to is not None:
        data.save(save_to)
    return data

@classmethod
def load(cls, filename, flux_dtype=None, zsun=None):
    """Load from HDF5; a 3-D grid without ``ssp_afe`` is promoted to n_afe = 1 at [alpha/Fe] = 0.
    ``zsun`` as for :meth:`SSPData.load`."""
    arrays, extra, meta = cls._read_h5(filename, flux_dtype=flux_dtype)
    ssp_afe = extra['ssp_afe']
    if ssp_afe is None:
        ssp_afe = jnp.zeros(1)
        arrays['ssp_flux'] = arrays['ssp_flux'][None, ...]
        if meta.get('ssp_stellar_mass') is not None:
            meta['ssp_stellar_mass'] = meta['ssp_stellar_mass'][None, ...]
    return cls(**arrays, ssp_afe=ssp_afe, **meta, zsun=zsun)

            "resolution_segments.  The sampling-floor provenance is "
            "recorded automatically; a source note only accompanies "
            "explicit library-LSF segments."
        )
    if resolution_segments is not None and resolution_source is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "from_fsps(): resolution_segments were given without "
            "resolution_source.  Cite where the LSF numbers come from "
            "— uncited resolution numbers must not ship in a released "
            "grid."
        )
    for bad in ('afe', 'afeindx'):
        if bad in fsps_kwargs:
            raise ValueError(
                f"from_fsps() rejects the FSPS kwarg {bad!r}: the "
                f"[alpha/Fe] axis is spanned by the grid itself "
                f"(ssp_afe); CSPBasis_afe samples it through "
                f"theta['afe'], so a fixed alpha must not be set at "
                f"build time."
            )
    kwargs = _validate_fsps_kwargs(fsps_kwargs)

    fsps = _import_fsps(
        "SSPDataAfe.load(ceridwen.ssps.fetch_grid('amist_c3k_hr_krou_afe'))")

    ssp = fsps.StellarPopulation(zcontinuous=0, sfh=0, **kwargs)

    n_afe = int(getattr(ssp, "n_afe", 1))
    if afe_values is not None:
        ssp_afe = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(afe_values, dtype=float))
        if ssp_afe.size != n_afe:
            raise ValueError(
                f"afe_values has {ssp_afe.size} entries but the "
                f"compiled FSPS grid has n_afe = {n_afe}."
            )
    elif n_afe == 5:
        ssp_afe = FSPS_AFE_VALUES_NAFE5.copy()
    elif n_afe == 1:
        ssp_afe = np.zeros(1)
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Compiled FSPS grid has n_afe = {n_afe}, which does not "
            f"match the documented aMIST/C3K layout (5) or a "
            f"solar-scaled build (1); pass afe_values= explicitly "
            f"(the [alpha/Fe] of each afeindx plane, in order)."
        )

    ssp_lgmet      = jnp.log10(ssp.zlegend)
    nzmet          = int(ssp_lgmet.size)
    ssp_lg_age_gyr = jnp.array(ssp.log_age - 9.0)

    planes = []
    mass_planes = []
    iso_planes = []
    _wave = None
    for afe_indx in range(1, n_afe + 1):               # afeindx is 1-based
        if n_afe > 1:
            ssp.params["afeindx"] = afe_indx
            print(f"[alpha/Fe] plane {afe_indx}/{n_afe} "
                  f"(afe = {ssp_afe[afe_indx - 1]:+.1f})")
        spectrum_collector = []
        mass_collector = []
        iso_collector = []
        for zmet_indx in range(1, nzmet + 1):
            print(f"...retrieving metallicity {zmet_indx}/{nzmet} "
                  f"[Z = {ssp.zlegend[zmet_indx - 1]:.4f}]")
            _wave, _fluxes = ssp.get_spectrum(
                tage=0.0, zmet=zmet_indx, peraa=False)
            spectrum_collector.append(_fluxes)
            mass_collector.append(np.array(ssp.stellar_mass, dtype=np.float64))
            iso_collector.append(isochrone_points_or_none(ssp))
        planes.append(np.array(spectrum_collector))
        mass_planes.append(np.array(mass_collector))
        iso_planes.append(iso_collector)

        _z_now = np.log10(np.asarray(ssp.zlegend))
        if not np.allclose(_z_now, np.asarray(ssp_lgmet)):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"zlegend changed between alpha planes (afeindx="
                f"{afe_indx}); the Z grids are ragged across "
                f"[alpha/Fe] and cannot form a rectangular "
                f"(afe, Z, age, wave) grid."
            )

    ssp_wave = jnp.array(_wave)
    ssp_flux = np.stack(planes, axis=0)                # host NumPy (SSPData keeps it there)

    meta = _read_fsps_provenance(ssp, kwargs, ssp_wave, ssp_lgmet)
    meta['schema_version'] = SSP_AFE_SCHEMA_VERSION
    iso = (None if iso_planes[0][0] is None
           else np.array(iso_planes, dtype=np.float64))
    meta['ssp_stellar_mass'], note = corrected_table(ssp, np.stack(mass_planes, axis=0), iso)
    meta['stellar_mass_source'] = fsps_stellar_mass_source(meta['fsps_version']) + note
    if n_afe > 1 and meta.get('isoc_type') == 'mist':
        meta['refused_cells'] = _duplicated_isochrone_cells(n_afe, int(nzmet))

    from .library_resolution import combined_sigma_v, combined_source
    sigma_v = combined_sigma_v(np.asarray(ssp_wave),
                               segments=resolution_segments)

    data = cls(ssp_lgmet, ssp_lg_age_gyr, ssp_wave, ssp_flux,
               ssp_afe=jnp.array(ssp_afe),
               ssp_resolution=sigma_v,
               resolution_source=combined_source(resolution_source),
               **meta)
    if save_to is not None:
        data.save(save_to)
    return data

def fetch_grid(name: str, *, force: bool = False, quiet: bool = False) -> Path:
    """Return a local, checksum-verified path to the registry grid ``name``,
    downloading into :func:`grid_cache_dir` on first use (``force`` re-downloads)."""
    if name not in REGISTRY:
        raise KeyError(
            f"Unknown grid {name!r}. Available: {sorted(REGISTRY)}."
        )
    entry = REGISTRY[name]
    if entry["url"] is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Grid {name!r} is defined but not yet published (no URL in the "
            f"registry). Notes: {entry['notes']}"
        )

    dest = grid_cache_dir() / f"{name}.h5"

    if dest.exists() and not force:
        _verify_cached(name, dest)
        return dest

    if not quiet:
        size = f" (~{entry['size_mb']} MB)" if entry.get("size_mb") else ""
        print(f"[ceridwen] fetching grid {name!r}{size} -> {dest}",
              file=sys.stderr)

    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=dest.parent, suffix=".part")
    os.close(fd)
    tmp = Path(tmp)
    try:
        _download(entry["url"], tmp)
        got = _sha256(tmp)
        if entry["sha256"] and got != entry["sha256"]:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Downloaded grid {name!r} fails its checksum "
                f"(got {got[:12]}..., expected {entry['sha256'][:12]}...). "
                f"The remote file changed or the download was corrupted; "
                f"not installing it."
            )
        tmp.replace(dest)
    finally:
        if tmp.exists():
            tmp.unlink()

    return dest

def logzsol_total(logzsol, afe, x: float = X_ALPHA_MIST25):
    """Total metallicity [Z/H] (Z/X definition) from ``logzsol`` = [Fe/H] on an alpha grid."""
    return logzsol + f_alpha(afe, x)

def f_alpha(afe, x: float = X_ALPHA_MIST25):
    """[Z/H] - [Fe/H] at [alpha/Fe] = ``afe`` (jnp- and numpy-compatible, differentiable)."""
    try:
        import jax.numpy as xp
    except ImportError:          # pragma: no cover
        xp = np
    return xp.log10(1.0 - x + x * 10.0 ** afe)

def chash_arrays(ssp_wave, ssp_lg_age_gyr, ssp_lgmet, ssp_flux, ssp_afe=None) -> str:
    """``chash-v1`` of a grid's arrays (see the module docstring)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    _update(h, "ssp_wave", ssp_wave)
    _update(h, "ssp_lg_age_gyr", ssp_lg_age_gyr)
    _update(h, "ssp_lgmet", ssp_lgmet)
    if ssp_afe is not None:
        _update(h, "ssp_afe", ssp_afe)
    _update(h, "ssp_flux", ssp_flux)
    return f"{CHASH_VERSION}:{h.hexdigest()}"

Composite stellar population basis. predict(theta, observations) projects the model onto observations.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default SSPData SSPData -- SSP grids (wave, flux, ages, metallicities, optional resolution curve). required theta dict -- initial values; must contain "lookback_time" (Gyr, increasing, index 0 = today,

= 2 nodes) and "sfh", plus "logzsol" (zh_const=True, shape (1,)) or "logzsol_hist" (zh_const=False, shape (n_time,)), both log10(Z/Z_sun) of the grid. Mutually exclusive with lookback_time=.

None lookback_time array -- shortcut for ``theta``: the node grid only, neutral initial values

(sfh = 1, metallicity = grid median).

None sfh_per_bin bool -- with ``lookback_time=``, one SFR per bin (n_time-1,) instead of per node. False zh_const bool -- constant metallicity ("logzsol") or a history ("logzsol_hist", one per node). False gas_tied bool -- gas-phase metallicity follows the stellar one, gas_logz := logzsol (or

logzsol_hist[0], today's value), as Prospector ties them; "gas_logz" is then not a parameter. The two are the SAME NUMBER, not the same absolute Z: logzsol uses the SSP grid's Z_sun (e.g. 0.0185 for MIST) and gas_logz the CLOUDY grid's own reference (Byler+2017; its node set is 0.019- or 0.020-based), which is the FSPS/Prospector convention.

False add_neb bool -- physics switches. True add_dust bool -- physics switches. True add_diffuse_dust bool -- physics switches. True add_dust_emission bool -- physics switches. True add_igm bool -- physics switches. True duste_model (DL07, THEMIS)

Draine & Li (2007) or THEMIS (Jones et al. 2013, 2017), both from $SPS_HOME/dust/dustem with FSPS's (qPAH, Umin) axes. THEMIS's duste_qpah axis spans 0.91-18.2 (the FSPS mass-fraction nodes x 100/2.2), DL07's 0.47-4.58.

'DL07' sps_home str -- data directory for the nebular and dust-emission grids; defaults to $SPS_HOME. None init_neb_params dict -- forwarded to NebularModel / Dust. ``isoc_type`` is

taken from the SSP grid's provenance when recorded. cloudy_dust (default False) picks the CLOUDY grids without dust in the H II region (ZAU_ND, the FSPS / Prospector default); True the dusty ones (ZAU_WD), whose lines differ from ND by a grid-dependent factor (constant SFH 0-1 Gyr, solar, logU -2.5: MIST H-alpha x0.78, Ly-alpha x0.17, [O III] 5007 x1.13; BPASS x0.95, x0.40, x0.99).

None init_dust_params dict -- forwarded to NebularModel / Dust. ``isoc_type`` is

taken from the SSP grid's provenance when recorded. cloudy_dust (default False) picks the CLOUDY grids without dust in the H II region (ZAU_ND, the FSPS / Prospector default); True the dusty ones (ZAU_WD), whose lines differ from ND by a grid-dependent factor (constant SFH 0-1 Gyr, solar, logU -2.5: MIST H-alpha x0.78, Ly-alpha x0.17, [O III] 5007 x1.13; BPASS x0.95, x0.40, x0.99).

None sfh_interp (step, linear)

piecewise-linear (analytic log-age integral, small negative weights clipped) SFH.

'step' track_zred_age bool -- with a sampled ``zred``, rescale the lookback grid so its oldest node

is the age of the Universe at that redshift, keeping the mass theta["sfh"] forms on the construction grid (the SFR is scaled by T_grid / age(zred)).

False fesc_geometry (runaway_bc, picket)

'runaway_bc': a fraction frac_obrun of EVERY age row skips that row's age-bin attenuation (the diffuse dust still applies); with several attenuated age bins old stars escape too. The nebular ages emit a fraction frac_obrun of their LyC and power 1 - frac_obrun of the nebular emission. 'picket': a fraction frac_obrun of the young light (the nebular grid's ages, young_mask), LyC included, meets no dust or gas at all (no age-bin or diffuse dust, no nebular reprocessing, no dust heating); needs add_neb=True.

'runaway_bc' cosmo Cosmology -- required; used for the flux factor and for the age of the Universe. None nebemlineinspec bool -- default of ``include_lines`` in ``get_spectrum`` only. False wavelength_support bool -- opt-in (default False): ``predict`` synthesises only the model

pixels the observations read (_support_for: Photometry's filter columns and sigma_gal window, a Spectrum's projector window) and zero-fills the rest after the mass, flux and IGM scaling; ~2.5-3x faster likelihood on CPU for a JWST photometry (+ grating) model on the 1 A - 1e8 A BPASS grid. Not byte-identical to the whole grid: XLA's reductions change their summation order with the array length, so predictions differ in the last float32 bit (relative ~1e-7). Ignored (whole grid) for dust emission, painted lines and a Photometry at a sampled redshift.

False agn ceridwen.agn.AGNConfig, True, a mode name, or None -- the AGN (Nenkova+08 torus,

Temple+21 disc, dust4 screen, narrow lines), off by default (None: every path unchanged, byte for byte). AGNConfig() / True = "corrected" (exact fagn * L_bol, clamped agn_tau, before the IGM, energy balance with dust emission); AGNConfig(agn_mode="fsps") / "fsps" reproduces FSPS add_agn_dust, "prospector" Prospector's AGNSSPBasis + AGNSpecModel; see ceridwen.agn and docs/agn.md. The theta keys (fagn, agn_tau, ...) get their defaults here.

def __init__(
    self,
    SSPData,
    theta=None,
    tiny_logt=-70,
    zh_const=False,
    add_neb=True,
    init_neb_params=None,
    nebemlineinspec=False,
    add_dust=True,
    add_diffuse_dust=True,
    add_dust_emission=False,
    add_igm=False,
    igm_model="madau1995",
    igm_factor=1.0,
    sps_home=None,
    init_dust_params=None,
    diffuse_law='kriek_conroy',
    verbose=True,
    sfh_interp='step',
    track_zred_age=False,
    lookback_time=None,
    sfh_per_bin=False,
    fesc_geometry="runaway_bc",
    duste_model="DL07",
    cosmo=None,
    gas_tied=False,
    wavelength_support=False,
    agn=None,
    **kwargs,
):
    self.verbose = bool(verbose)
    self.gas_tied = bool(gas_tied)
    self._wave_support = bool(wavelength_support)
    if self.gas_tied and not add_neb:
        raise ValueError("gas_tied=True ties the nebular gas metallicity to the stars, "
                         "but add_neb=False: there is no nebular model to tie")
    if kwargs:
        hint = ""
        if "sigma_losvd_kms" in kwargs:
            hint = (" ('sigma_losvd_kms' is not an argument: the galaxy velocity "
                    "dispersion is set once on the model, "
                    "SedModel(kinematics=Kinematics(sigma_gal=...)))")
        elif "tuniv" in kwargs:
            hint = (" ('tuniv' is not an argument: the age of the Universe comes from "
                    "the cosmology, csp.age_at(z) / cosmo.age(z))")
        raise TypeError(
            f"CSPBasis got unexpected keyword argument(s) {sorted(kwargs)}{hint}")
    if lookback_time is not None:
        if theta is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Pass either theta= (full control over the initial "
                "parameter values) or the lookback_time= shortcut, not "
                "both."
            )
        _lb = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.asarray(lookback_time, dtype=float))
        _n = int(_lb.size)
        theta = {
            'lookback_time': _lb,
            'sfh': jnp.ones(max(_n - 1, 1) if sfh_per_bin else _n),
        }
        _lz_mid = _default_logzsol(SSPData)
        if zh_const:
            theta['logzsol'] = jnp.array([_lz_mid])
        else:
            theta['logzsol_hist'] = jnp.full((_n,), _lz_mid)
    if theta is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "CSPBasis needs the static SFH grid structure. Pass either\n"
            "  lookback_time=jnp.linspace(0.0, T_oldest, n_nodes)   "
            "(shortcut; neutral initial values), or\n"
            "  theta={'lookback_time': ..., 'sfh': ..., 'logzsol' or 'logzsol_hist': ...} "
            "(full control).\n"
            "lookback_time is in Gyr, monotonically increasing, index 0 = "
            "today, >= 2 nodes."
        )
    # copies: initialize_neb pops / adds keys, and the caller may reuse the dict (B1-015)
    init_neb_params = {"cloudy_dust": False, **(init_neb_params or {})}
    init_dust_params = ({'bin_edges': [(-jnp.inf, -1.97)], 'laws': ['powerlaw']}
                        if init_dust_params is None else dict(init_dust_params))

    # the grid's cube is host NumPy; the float32 cast runs on the device (XLA's convert,
    # which flushes float32 subnormals, as before) from a transient float64 copy that is
    # freed at once, so the device keeps only the float32 cube
    _f64 = jnp.asarray(SSPData.ssp_flux)
    self.flux      = _f64.astype(jnp.float32)          # (n_z, n_age, n_wave)
    del _f64
    self.wave      = jnp.array(SSPData.ssp_wave)       # (n_wave,)
    # the attenuation curves are evaluated on this float32 copy: the kernels use them in
    # float32 (the wavelengths that place lines and pixels stay float64, self.wave)
    self._wave32   = self.wave.astype(jnp.float32)
    self.ages      = jnp.array(SSPData.ssp_lg_age_gyr) # (n_age,)  log10(Gyr)
    self._setup_metallicity(SSPData)                   # self.zmet: logzsol axis
    self.lib_resolution = (
        (np.asarray(SSPData.ssp_wave, dtype=np.float64),
         np.asarray(SSPData.ssp_resolution, dtype=np.float64))
        if getattr(SSPData, "ssp_resolution", None) is not None else None)
    self.ssp_ages_lgyr = self.ages + 9                 # log10(yr)
    # surviving mass per M_sun formed (SSP schema 3); post-processing only, never traced
    # by the forward model
    _m = getattr(SSPData, "ssp_stellar_mass", None)
    self.ssp_stellar_mass = None if _m is None else np.asarray(_m, dtype=np.float64)
    self.stellar_mass_source = getattr(SSPData, "stellar_mass_source", None)
    self.stellar_mass_refused = getattr(SSPData, "stellar_mass_refused", None)

    self._ssp_isoc_type    = getattr(SSPData, "isoc_type", None)
    self._ssp_spec_library = getattr(SSPData, "spec_library", None)
    self._ssp_imf_type     = getattr(SSPData, "imf_type", None)   # FSPS imf_type (display only)

    if fesc_geometry not in ("runaway_bc", "picket"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"fesc_geometry must be 'runaway_bc' or 'picket', got {fesc_geometry!r}")
    if fesc_geometry == "picket" and not add_neb:
        raise ValueError(
            "fesc_geometry='picket' needs add_neb=True: its clear channel is defined on the "
            "ages of the nebular (CLOUDY) grid and the covered ionising photons power the "
            "nebular emission.  Without a nebular model use fesc_geometry='runaway_bc'.")
    self.fesc_geometry = str(fesc_geometry)

    self._logage_lo  = self.ssp_ages_lgyr[1:]
    self._logage_hi  = self.ssp_ages_lgyr[:-1]
    self._dlogage    = jnp.diff(self.ssp_ages_lgyr)
    self._j_range    = jnp.arange(self.ssp_ages_lgyr.size)
    self._age_clip_lo = 10.0 ** (-70)                  # floor for log-time clipping
    self._age_clip_hi = 10.0 ** self.ssp_ages_lgyr[-1] # ceiling
    self._n_z   = len(self.zmet)
    self._n_age = len(self.ages)

    self._ssp_lo_yr = 10.0 ** self._logage_hi   # (n_age-1,)
    self._ssp_hi_yr = 10.0 ** self._logage_lo   # (n_age-1,)

    _ssp_age_yr  = 10.0 ** self.ssp_ages_lgyr           # (n_age,) linear yr
    _voro_mid    = 0.5 * (_ssp_age_yr[:-1] + _ssp_age_yr[1:])  # (n_age-1,)
    _voro_hi_ext = _ssp_age_yr[-1] + (_ssp_age_yr[-1] - _ssp_age_yr[-2])
    self._ssp_voronoi_lo = jnp.concatenate(
        [jnp.zeros(1), _voro_mid]
    )
    self._ssp_voronoi_hi = jnp.concatenate(
        [_voro_mid, jnp.array([_voro_hi_ext])]
    )

    self.tiny_logt  = tiny_logt
    if sps_home is None:
        sps_home = os.environ.get("SPS_HOME")
    if (add_neb or add_dust_emission) and not sps_home:
        raise ValueError(
            "sps_home is required for nebular / dust emission but was not "
            "given and $SPS_HOME is unset. Set `export SPS_HOME=/path/to/fsps` "
            "(your FSPS data directory) or pass sps_home=... explicitly."
        )
    self.sps_home   = sps_home
    self.duste_model = _check_duste_model(duste_model, add_dust_emission)
    from ..cosmology import Cosmology as _Cosmology
    if cosmo is None:
        raise TypeError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} needs an explicit cosmology: pass "
            "cosmo=Cosmology.planck18(), Cosmology.wmap9(), "
            "Cosmology.flat(H0, Om0), Cosmology.from_name(...) or "
            "Cosmology.from_astropy(...)  (from ceridwen import Cosmology)")
    if not isinstance(cosmo, _Cosmology):
        raise TypeError(
            f"cosmo must be a ceridwen Cosmology, got {type(cosmo).__name__}; "
            "for an astropy cosmology use Cosmology.from_astropy(...)")
    self._cosmo = cosmo
    self.track_zred_age = bool(track_zred_age)
    self.nebemlineinspec = bool(nebemlineinspec)

    self._setup_igm(add_igm, igm_model, igm_factor)

    if add_diffuse_dust or add_dust:
        self.set_attenuation_function(add_diffuse_dust, add_dust)

    theta = self.initialize_dust_components(
        add_dust, add_diffuse_dust, add_dust_emission,
        theta, init_dust_params, diffuse_law, sps_home,
    )
    theta = self.initialize_neb(add_neb, theta, init_neb_params, sps_home)

    self.configure_spectrum_model(
        add_dust, add_diffuse_dust, add_dust_emission, add_neb, sps_home
    )
    theta = self._install_agn(agn, theta, SSPData, add_dust_emission, sps_home)

    if sfh_interp not in ('step', 'linear'):
        raise ValueError(
            f"sfh_interp must be 'step' or 'linear', got {sfh_interp!r}"
        )
    self.sfh_interp = sfh_interp
    self.zh_const = bool(zh_const)
    if zh_const:
        if sfh_interp == 'step':
            self.calculate_ssp_weights = self.calculate_ssp_weights_const_zh_step
        else:
            self.calculate_ssp_weights = self.calculate_ssp_weights_const_zh
    else:
        if sfh_interp == 'step':
            self.calculate_ssp_weights = self.calculate_ssp_weights_var_zh_step
        else:
            self.calculate_ssp_weights = self.calculate_ssp_weights_var_zh
    if verbose:
        print(f"SFH integration scheme : {sfh_interp}")

    self.initialize_model_structure(theta)

    if verbose:
        print("\nCSPBasis (dict theta) — registered parameters:")
        pprint.pprint({k: v.shape for k, v in self.theta_init.items()})

    self.check_param_ranges(self.theta_init)

def initialize_model_structure(self, theta):
    """Validate ``theta`` (grid, sfh shape, metallicity key) and build ``theta_init`` / ``param_names``."""
    if 'lookback_time' not in theta:
        raise ValueError(
            "theta must contain 'lookback_time' — the static SFH node grid "
            "(Gyr, monotonically increasing, index 0 = today). It is "
            "required even when the redshift is a free parameter: with "
            "track_zred_age=True the grid is rescaled inside the forward "
            "pass to track age(zred), but its LENGTH and RELATIVE spacing "
            "come from this construction-time grid, so it defines n_time "
            "and the bin structure rather than a fixed absolute age range."
        )
    if 'sfh' not in theta:
        raise ValueError(
            "theta must contain 'sfh' — star-formation-rate values, either "
            "one per lookback node (shape (n_time,)) or one per bin "
            "(shape (n_time-1,), FastStepBasis convention), where n_time = "
            "len(theta['lookback_time'])."
        )

    self.sfh_times = jnp.atleast_1d(
        jnp.asarray(theta['lookback_time'], dtype=float)
    ) * 1e9   # Gyr → yr
    self.n_time = self.sfh_times.size

    if self.n_time < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"theta['lookback_time'] has {self.n_time} node(s); at least "
            "2 are required (n_time nodes define n_time-1 SFH bins). "
            "Typical fits use 5-10 nodes, e.g. "
            "jnp.linspace(0.0, T_UNIV, 6)."
        )

    _lb = np.asarray(self.sfh_times, dtype=np.float64)
    _diffs = np.diff(_lb)
    if not (np.all(_diffs > 0.0) and _lb[0] >= 0.0 and _lb[0] < 1e8):
        raise ValueError(
            "theta['lookback_time'] must be monotonically *increasing*:\n"
            f"  - index 0 = today (≈ 0 Gyr): got {_lb[0]/1e9:.3f} Gyr\n"
            f"  - index -1 = oldest (≈ T_univ): got {_lb[-1]/1e9:.3f} Gyr\n"
            f"  - first three values [Gyr]: {(_lb[:3]/1e9).tolist()}\n"
            "If your grid runs from oldest to today, replace e.g.\n"
            "    lookback = T_UNIV - jnp.linspace(eps, T_UNIV, N)\n"
            "with\n"
            "    lookback = jnp.linspace(0.0, T_UNIV, N)\n"
            "and reverse theta['sfh'] (and theta['logzsol_hist'] if present) to match."
        )

    sfh = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.asarray(theta['sfh'], dtype=float))
    if sfh.shape == (self.n_time,):
        self.sfh_per_bin = False
    elif sfh.shape == (self.n_time - 1,):
        self.sfh_per_bin = True
    else:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"'sfh' shape {sfh.shape} must be either "
            f"({self.n_time},)  (node-based, legacy)  or "
            f"({self.n_time - 1},)  (per-bin, FastStepBasis)."
        )

    sfh_np = np.asarray(sfh)
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(sfh_np)):
        raise ValueError(
            "theta['sfh'] contains non-finite (NaN/Inf) values; this would "
            "silently produce a NaN spectrum."
        )
    if np.any(sfh_np < 0):
        warnings.warn(
            "theta['sfh'] contains negative values. SFR is clipped to >=0 "
            "internally, so negative bins contribute ~zero flux (no error is "
            "raised at evaluation time).",
            stacklevel=3,
        )

    for old in REMOVED_METALLICITY_KEYS:
        if old in theta:
            raise removed_metallicity_key_error(old, theta[old], self.log10_zsun,
                                                self.axis_meaning)
    if self.zh_const:
        if 'logzsol' not in theta:
            raise ValueError(
                "zh_const=True requires a constant metallicity theta['logzsol'] "
                "(shape-(1,) array, log10(Z/Z_sun) of the SSP grid, e.g. 0.0 = solar); "
                "none was provided. Either add theta['logzsol'], or construct with "
                "zh_const=False and provide a history theta['logzsol_hist'] of shape "
                "(n_time,)."
            )
        if 'logzsol_hist' in theta:
            raise ValueError(
                "zh_const=True but theta also contains 'logzsol_hist'; a constant-"
                "metallicity basis reads only 'logzsol'. Remove 'logzsol_hist' or "
                "construct with zh_const=False.")
    else:
        if 'logzsol_hist' not in theta:
            raise ValueError(
                "zh_const=False requires a metallicity history theta['logzsol_hist'] "
                "of shape (n_time,) (log10(Z/Z_sun) of the SSP grid, one per lookback "
                "node, index 0 = today); none was provided. Either add it, or "
                "construct with zh_const=True and provide theta['logzsol']."
            )
        if 'logzsol' in theta:
            raise ValueError(
                "zh_const=False but theta also contains 'logzsol'; a metallicity-"
                "history basis reads only 'logzsol_hist'. Remove 'logzsol' or "
                "construct with zh_const=True.")
    if self.gas_tied and 'gas_logz' in theta:
        raise ValueError(
            "gas_tied=True sets gas_logz from the stellar logzsol, but theta also "
            "gives 'gas_logz'; remove one (a tied gas metallicity is not a parameter).")

    self.zh_is_scalar = None
    if 'logzsol_hist' in theta:
        zh = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.asarray(theta['logzsol_hist'], dtype=float))
        assert zh.shape == (self.n_time,), "'logzsol_hist' must match 'lookback_time' length"
        self.zh_is_scalar = False
    elif 'logzsol' in theta:
        Z = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.asarray(theta['logzsol'], dtype=float))
        assert Z.shape == (1,), "'logzsol' must be a scalar (wrapped in shape-(1,) array)"
        self.zh_is_scalar = True


    self.theta_init = {}
    for k, v in theta.items():
        if k == 'lookback_time':
            continue   # static grid — not a free parameter
        arr = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.asarray(v, dtype=float))
        self.theta_init[k] = arr

    self.theta_init['sfh'] = sfh

    self.param_names = list(self.theta_init.keys())

    self._known_theta_keys = set(self.param_names) | {
        'lookback_time', 'logzsol', 'logzsol_hist',
        'logmass', 'zred', 'lumdist_mpc', 'igm_factor', 'eline_scaling',
        'frac_obrun', 'spectrum_scaling', 'spectrum_calib',
    } | set(getattr(getattr(self, "igm", None), "param_names", ())) \
      | set(getattr(self._agn, "param_names", ()))

def check_param_ranges(self, theta=None, warn=True):
    """Messages (and warnings) for metallicity / nebular parameters outside the interpolation grids, where the model clamps silently."""
    if theta is None:
        theta = self.theta_init
    msgs = []

    for old in REMOVED_METALLICITY_KEYS:
        if old in theta:
            raise removed_metallicity_key_error(old, theta[old], self.log10_zsun,
                                                self.axis_meaning)
    zlo, zhi = float(self.zmet.min()), float(self.zmet.max())
    zs = (f"Z_sun = {self.zsun_nominal:.6g}, log10 Z_sun = {self.log10_zsun:.6f}"
          if self.zsun_nominal is not None else f"log10 Z_sun = {self.log10_zsun:.6f}")
    for key in LOGZSOL_KEYS:
        if key in theta:
            v = np.asarray(theta[key], float)
            if v.size and (np.nanmin(v) < zlo or np.nanmax(v) > zhi):
                msgs.append(
                    f"theta['{key}'] = {np.array2string(v, precision=3)} is outside the "
                    f"SSP metallicity grid, logzsol in [{zlo:+.3f}, {zhi:+.3f}] "
                    f"({zs}); the interpolation clamps to the edge node there."
                )
            if v.size and np.nanmax(v) < ABSOLUTE_LOOKING_LOGZSOL:
                msgs.append(
                    f"theta['{key}'] = {np.array2string(v, precision=3)} is below "
                    f"{ABSOLUTE_LOOKING_LOGZSOL} everywhere: is it an OLD absolute log10 Z? "
                    f"logzsol = log10(Z/Z_sun) is 0 at solar on this grid ({zs}); an "
                    f"absolute log10 Z = {float(np.nanmax(v)):+.3f} would be logzsol = "
                    f"{float(np.nanmax(v)) - self.log10_zsun:+.3f}.  Ignore this if a "
                    "metal-poor population is intended."
                )

    neb = getattr(self, 'neb', None)
    if neb is not None:
        for key, attrs in (
            ('gas_logz', ('logZ_grid', 'logz_grid', '_logZ', 'nebem_logz')),
            ('gas_logu', ('logU_grid', 'logu_grid', '_logU', 'nebem_logu')),
        ):
            if key == 'gas_logz' and self.gas_tied:
                src = 'logzsol' if self.zh_const else 'logzsol_hist'
                if src not in theta:
                    continue
                g = np.asarray(neb.nebem_logz, float)
                v = np.asarray(theta[src], float)
                v = v if self.zh_const else v[:1]
                if v.size and (np.nanmin(v) < g.min() or np.nanmax(v) > g.max()):
                    msgs.append(
                        f"gas_tied=True: the gas metallicity follows theta['{src}'] = "
                        f"{np.array2string(v, precision=3)}, outside the nebular grid "
                        f"[{g.min():.3f}, {g.max():.3f}] (log10 Z_gas/Z_sun of the "
                        "CLOUDY grid); the nebular emission clamps there.")
                continue
            if key in theta:
                grid = next((getattr(neb, a) for a in attrs if hasattr(neb, a)),
                            None)
                if grid is not None:
                    g = np.asarray(grid, float)
                    glo, ghi = float(g.min()), float(g.max())
                    v = np.asarray(theta[key], float)
                    if v.size and (np.nanmin(v) < glo or np.nanmax(v) > ghi):
                        msgs.append(
                            f"theta['{key}'] = {np.array2string(v, precision=3)} outside "
                            f"the nebular grid [{glo:.3f}, {ghi:.3f}]"
                            + (" (log10 Z_gas/Z_sun of the CLOUDY grid)"
                               if key == 'gas_logz' else "")
                            + "; the nebular emission clamps there."
                        )

    if self._agn is not None:
        msgs += self._agn.range_messages(theta)

    if warn:
        for m in msgs:
            warnings.warn(m, stacklevel=2)
    return msgs

def set_attenuation_function(self, add_diffuse_dust, add_dust):
    """Assign ``self.attenuate_dust(wave, theta) -> (attn_birthcloud (n_bins, n_wave), attn_diffuse (n_wave,))`` as optical depths.

    The attribute is a BOUND METHOD of this instance (one of ``_attenuate_*``), not a closure
    over ``self``: a shallow copy whose stored bound methods are re-bound to the copy then
    reads the COPY's dust models.  The expressions are unchanged (bit-identical).  It is set
    only when dust is configured, so ``hasattr(csp, "attenuate_dust")`` keeps meaning
    "this CSP attenuates" (``model.py``, ``_agn_galaxy_ldust``)."""
    if add_diffuse_dust and add_dust:
        if self.verbose:
            print("Using combined (binwise + diffuse) dust attenuation.")
        self.attenuate_dust = types.MethodType(CSPBasis._attenuate_bc_and_diffuse, self)

    elif add_dust and not add_diffuse_dust:
        if self.verbose:
            print("Using only binwise dust attenuation.")
        self.attenuate_dust = types.MethodType(CSPBasis._attenuate_bc_only, self)

    elif add_diffuse_dust and not add_dust:
        self.bin_low  = jnp.array([-jnp.inf])
        self.bin_high = jnp.array([jnp.inf])
        if self.verbose:
            print("Using only diffuse dust attenuation.")
        self.attenuate_dust = types.MethodType(CSPBasis._attenuate_diffuse_only, self)

def get_spectrum_components(self, theta: dict) -> tuple:
    """``(continuum, lines)`` on the rest-frame grid, unscaled (no mass, distance or IGM):
    ``continuum`` is ``get_spectrum(include_lines=False)`` and ``lines`` the difference to the
    full spectrum: the attenuated painted lines.  With dust emission the dust re-emission of
    the lines' absorbed energy is in ``continuum``, as on every path.
    """
    self._warn_unknown_theta_keys(theta)
    continuum = self.get_spectrum(theta=theta, include_lines=False)
    full      = self.get_spectrum(theta=theta, include_lines=True)
    return continuum, full - continuum

def predict(self, theta: dict, observations: list, *, kinematics=None,
            broaden_photometry=False, eline_system=None) -> dict:
    """``{obs.name: prediction}``: Photometry -> maggies (n_filters,), Spectrum -> F_nu [erg/s/cm^2/Hz]
    on the observed pixels, Lines -> integrated fluxes (n_lines,).  Observed-frame only when
    ``theta`` carries ``zred``.

    ``kinematics`` (``Kinematics`` or None) supplies sigma_gal / sigma_gas; ``broaden_photometry``
    applies them to the spectrum entering each Photometry's ``_broadener``.  Lines are painted on
    the model grid only when a consumer needs them there (free-z Photometry, Photometry with a
    sampled sigma_gas and ``broaden_photometry``, or ``_force_paint_lines``); otherwise fixed-z
    Photometry adds them through the static basis ``G = obs._T @ (IGM * profiles)``, Spectrum
    paints them on the observed pixels and Lines reads them from the grid.

    ``eline_system`` (``ElineSystem`` of ``SedModel``, line marginalisation): returns
    ``(predictions, aux)`` with the fitted lines removed from every prediction and
    ``aux = {"prior_mean": CLOUDY fluxes of the fitted lines, "cols": {obs.name: design}}``.
    """
    from ..observation.observation import (
        Spectrum as _Spectrum, Photometry as _Photometry,
    )
    if kinematics is not None:
        self._known_theta_keys |= set(kinematics.free_keys)
    has_neb = getattr(self, "neb", None) is not None
    gas_free = (kinematics is not None
                and isinstance(kinematics.effective_sigma_gas, str))
    paint_lines = has_neb and (
        getattr(self, "_force_paint_lines", False)
        or any(
            isinstance(o, _Photometry)
            and ((getattr(o, "free_z", False) and "zred" in theta)
                 or (gas_free and broaden_photometry))
            for o in observations
        )
    )
    support = self._support_for(observations, theta, paint_lines)
    if support is None:
        cont, lines = self._assemble_components(theta, paint_lines)
    else:
        self._warn_unknown_theta_keys(theta)
        cont = self.get_spectrum(theta=theta, include_lines=False, support=support)
        lines = None
    # mass and flux factor first; the IGM separately, so the kinematic kernels can act
    # before it (galaxy kinematics -> redshift -> IGM -> instrument)
    cont0, lines0 = self._apply_mass_redshift_igm(
        cont, cont if lines is None else lines, theta, igm=False)
    trans = None
    agn_corr = None
    if self.igm is not None and "zred" in theta:
        trans = self._igm_transmission(
            jnp.ravel(theta["zred"])[0], theta).astype(cont0.dtype)
        # on the whole grid, then the support: Madau's tau is capped at its peak (argmax)
        trans = _sel(trans, support)
        cont, lines_s = cont0 * trans, lines0 * trans
        agn_corr = self._agn_after_igm(theta, trans, cont0.dtype, support)
        if agn_corr is not None:
            cont = cont + agn_corr
    else:
        cont, lines_s = cont0, lines0
    if support is not None:
        # zeros on the pixels no observation reads, only after every scaling (XLA CPU
        # returns zeros for a pad inside that fusion)
        width = (support.start, self.wave.shape[0] - support.stop)
        cont, cont0 = jnp.pad(cont, width), jnp.pad(cont0, width)
        if agn_corr is not None:
            agn_corr = jnp.pad(agn_corr, width)
    return self._project_observations(
        cont if lines is None else cont + lines_s, cont,
        observations, theta, paint_lines=paint_lines,
        line_component=None if lines is None else lines_s,
        kinematics=kinematics, broaden_photometry=broaden_photometry,
        eline_system=eline_system,
        before_igm=None if trans is None else (cont0, None if lines is None else lines0),
        **({} if agn_corr is None else {"agn_after_igm": agn_corr}),
    )

Observed-frame fluxes of every nebular grid line (n_lines,), through the same weights, dust, escape, mass and distance factors as the spectrum.

Default: integrated fluxes [erg/s/cm^2] with the 1/(1+z) Jacobian, the IGM transmission averaged over the line's painted profile and eline_scaling (the Lines observation). for_spectrum: the same without eline_scaling (painted by the Spectrum projector). for_photometry: per-Hz amplitudes with the full f_nu flux factor and no IGM (applied inside the photometric line basis) and no eline_scaling.
